info.title: Applicamp API
info.description: The Applicamp HTTP API. Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Operations either are public or take the web app's session cookie (`session`); unsafe methods also need the `X-Applicamp-CSRF: 1` header and the app's own `Origin`.

get.description: Version 0 and no answers until they answer a question.

put.description:
All the answers at once, as the interview or an edit leaves them; a
question left out is unanswered. Values are trimmed and blank ones
removed. Lists over their limit (5 roles; 10 places, things to avoid and
must-haves), a currency that is not ISO 4217 or a choice that does not
exist are refused. Every save, even of the same answers, is a new version.

200.description: The goals, saved, at their new version.

get.description:
The account behind the session cookie, with the providers linked to it.
Never a token.

Every opportunity of the signed-in person, newest first, except the
dismissed ones ("Not for me") and the hidden ones (they fail a hard
requirement; `hidden=true` lists only those, with the reason). Filter by
stage, by text in the role, company or place, or to the new ones.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only those whose role, company or place contains this.

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: Only the new ones (Found, never opened).

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description:
Only the hidden ones: found before the requirement rules, they fail
one. Left out otherwise.

post.summary: Add a job by its link.
post.description:
A Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby posting is read from the board's public API
(title, company, place, pay, description), and that company's board is
searched from then on. Any other link becomes an opportunity with the
link and the title and company given (typed later if not): the server
never fetches it. The same posting twice answers the one already there
(200).

200.description: That posting was already in the pipeline.

get.description:
One of the signed-in person's, dismissed ones included. Anyone else's is
not found.

patch.description:
Its stage, next step, notes, "Not for me" (`dismissed`), or that it was
opened (no longer new). Title, company and place can be typed only for
one added by a link to a site that is not a job board.

409.description: `not_editable`: its title, company and place come from the job board

get.description: Empty (and no `source`) until they import or write one.

put.description:
The whole profile, as edited by hand. Values are trimmed and empty ones
removed; a value over its length, a date not like `2020`, `2020-03` or
`2020-03-15`, or a list of more than 200 entries is refused.

post.description:
A `multipart/form-data` upload of `kind` and either `file` (a LinkedIn
export ZIP, up to 20 MB; a PDF, up to 8 MB) or `text` (up to 60 000
characters). The answer is a draft to review: the profile is unchanged
until the draft is applied. The file is not kept.

A ZIP is read from its CSVs without any model; it is refused before
anything is extracted when it holds more than 200 files, a file over
5 MB or more than 50 MB uncompressed, or a path leaving the archive.
A PDF's text and pasted text are structured by the `complete` model, and
every value the source does not say is dropped and counted (`dropped`).

503.description: `ai_unavailable`: no model to read a PDF or text (import the LinkedIn ZIP instead); `ai_daily_limit_reached`; `ai_failed`

get.description:
One of the signed-in person's imports, until it expires. Anyone else's
is not found.

post.description:
`replace` makes the draft the profile; `merge` keeps the profile as it
is (hand edits included) and adds what the draft has that it does not.
Once applied, a draft cannot be applied again.

The profile is unchanged. Discarding twice is fine; an applied draft
cannot be discarded.

Reads the job boards, keeps the jobs within the goals' hard limits,
scores the best 40 against the profile and goals, and adds the good
matches as Found; follow it with `GET /api/v1/searches/latest`. At most
3 a day and one every 15 minutes (the instance may set others), never
past the spending limits.

202.description: Started; it runs in the background.

409.description: `profile_needed`: set up the profile and answer a goals question first; `search_running`: one is already running

429.description: `search_limit_reached`: the detail says when to try again

503.description: `ai_unavailable`: no model is set up; `ai_budget_reached`: a spending limit is reached

get.summary: About what a search would cost.
get.description:
The jobs it would likely score (the last search's, at most 40), times
what a batch of ten has cost this person on average, in euros; and what
they spent today and this month against their limits. Over €0.05 the
app asks before searching.

The signed-in person's newest search, running or done: how many jobs it
read, kept, scored and added, why it stopped if it did, and its cost.

How far the signed-in person is with their profile and goals, how many
new matches wait for them, their latest search, and the next step.

Checks `state` against the login cookie, redeems the code, validates the
ID token, and signs the person in if their provider identity is linked
or their verified address is on the invite list: a session cookie and a
redirect to `/`. Someone not on the list lands on `/not-invited`; any
failure on `/sign-in?error=sign_in_failed`. The login cookie is cleared
either way.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The `state` sent with the authorization request.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: An error code instead of a code.

303.description: To `/` signed in (with the session cookie), to `/not-invited`, or to `/sign-in?error=sign_in_failed`.

get.description: Only the configured ones; the sign-in page shows one button each.

get.summary: Start signing in with a provider.
get.description:
Seals a new sign-in (`state`, `nonce`, PKCE verifier) into a
ten-minute, `SameSite=Lax` login cookie and redirects to the provider's
authorization endpoint.

303.description: To the provider, or to `/sign-in?error=provider_unavailable` when it cannot be reached.

post.description:
Deletes the session on the server and clears the cookie. Needs the
`X-Applicamp-CSRF: 1` header and a same-origin request, like every
unsafe request.

204.description: Signed out (also when there was no session).

get.description: `ok` when the server answers and reaches its database.

mode.description: Replace the profile, or merge into it.

ApplyMode.description: How a draft reaches the profile.

Autonomy.description:
How much agents may do alone. Applying and emailing always wait for the
person, whatever this says.

location.description: Where they are, as written ("Lisbon, Portugal").

CashFloor.description: The least they would take, before tax.

Fact.description: What a posting says about a fact a requirement is checked on.

Goals.description: The answers to the goals interview. Nothing is required.

oneOf.description: How much agents may do alone.

avoid.description: What they will not work on (up to 10).

oneOf.description: The least they would take, before tax.

equity_counts.description: Whether equity counts toward the cash floor.

languages_for_work.description: The languages they can work in, as BCP 47 tags (`en`, `pt-PT`).

locations.description: Where they can work from: cities, countries or regions (up to 10).

must_have.description: What the job must have (up to 10).

oneOf.description: Whether they would move for the right job.

roles.description: The roles they want next (up to 5).

GoalsView.description: The goals and the version they are at.

version.description: 0 until something is saved; each save adds one.

HiddenReason.description: Why an opportunity is hidden: it fails a hard requirement.

Import.description: A draft profile waiting for review.

dropped.description:
Values left out of the draft: ones a model gave that the file does
not say (the source check), or that did not fit.

expires_at.description: When the draft is deleted if it is not applied.

ImportKind.description: What an import is made from.

ImportUpload.description:
An upload (`multipart/form-data`): the kind, then the file (ZIP or PDF)
or the text.

file.description: The file, for `linkedin_zip` (up to 20 MB) and `pdf` (up to 8 MB).

JobFacts.description:
What the posting says about the person's requirements, as their search
read it: "Remote · open to you · English".

open_to_candidate.description: Someone where the person lives can do it without moving.

region_note.description: Where it is open, as the posting says ("Germany or Austria only").

remote.description: It can be done fully remote.

email.description: The verified address the account was created with.

name.description: Their name, as their first way in gave it.

picture_url.description: Their photo, if a provider gave one.

ways_in.description: The providers that sign them in.

NewOpportunity.description: A job to add by its link.

company.description: The company, for a link to a site that is not a job board.

title.description: The role, for a link to a site that is not a job board.

url.description: The posting's address (http or https, up to 2 000 characters).

Opportunity.description: An opportunity, whole: what the side peek shows.

description.description: The posting's description, as plain text (up to 20 000 characters).

dismissed.description: "Not for me": hidden from the pipeline.

editable.description:
Title, company and location can be typed (an opportunity added by a
link to a site that is not a job board).

oneOf.description:
What the posting says about their requirements; none when never
checked (added by link, or found before the rules and not yet
checked).

gaps.description: What the profile or goals miss (up to 3).

oneOf.description: Why it is hidden, if it is: it fails a hard requirement.

match.description:
How well it matches the profile and goals, 0–100; none for one added
by link.

why.description: Why it matches, citing the profile (up to 3).

OpportunityChanges.description: What to change; anything left out stays as it is.

company.description: The company; only for one added by link to another site.

dismissed.description: "Not for me" (`true`) or back in the pipeline (`false`).

location.description: Where; only for one added by link to another site.

next_step.description: The next step (up to 300 characters); `null` clears it.

notes.description: The notes (up to 10 000 characters); `null` clears them.

opened.description: It was opened: it is no longer new.

title.description: The role; only for one added by link to another site.

opportunities.description:
Newest first; never the dismissed ones, and the hidden ones only when
asked for.

OpportunitySummary.description: An opportunity, as the table, the board and the list show it.

oneOf.description: Why it is hidden, if it is: it fails a hard requirement.

match.description:
How well it matches the profile and goals, 0–100; none for one added
by link.

region_note.description: Where it is open, as the posting says, to go with the reason.

Period.description: What a cash floor is counted over.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason (`not_found`, `session_required`, …).
Match and translate on this, never on `title` or `detail`.

detail.description: What went wrong in this occurrence, in English.

title.description: Short summary: the HTTP status's reason phrase.

type.description:
URI identifying the problem type; `about:blank` when the HTTP status
says it all.

example.detail: This resource does not exist, or you cannot see it.
example.title: Not Found

ProfileSource.description: Where the profile came from last.

ProfileView.description: The profile, and what can be imported into it.

import_kinds.description:
What this instance can import: always the LinkedIn export; PDFs and
text only when a model is configured for them.

profile.description: The profile; empty until something is imported or written.

oneOf.description: Where it came from last (the last import applied, or `manual`).

Providers.description: The sign-in providers this instance offers.

providers.description: In the order the sign-in page shows them.

Relocate.description: Whether they would move for the right job.

cost_eur.description: What its model calls cost, in euros.

dropped.description:
Jobs scored that fail a requirement (remote only, where they live,
a language, the pay floor): never added, whatever their score.

kept.description: Jobs within the goals' hard limits and not already in the pipeline.

scored.description: Jobs scored (by the model now, or before).

oneOf.description: Why it stopped early, if it did.

SearchEstimate.description: About what a search would cost now.

cost_eur.description: About what that costs, in euros.

SearchStatus.description: Where a search is. The same as the search's own (`sources`).

SearchStop.description: Why a search stopped early. The same as the search's own (`sources`).

SearchTrigger.description: What started a search. The same as the search's own (`sources`).

Spend.description: What was spent on AI, in euros, against the limits.

StrengthHint.description: What would make the profile stronger.

new_matches.description: Found opportunities never opened (hidden ones not counted).

done.description: There is a profile with something in it.

oneOf.description: What would make it stronger, if anything.
Why it stopped early, if it did.

endDate.description: As `startDate`; none while it is their current position.

session.name: __Host-applicamp_session
session.description: The web app's session cookie, set by `/bff/callback/{provider}` (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`; named `applicamp_session` when the instance's public URL is plain http). Unsafe methods also need the `X-Applicamp-CSRF: 1` header and the app's own `Origin`.

tags.name: identity
tags.description: Accounts and their ways in (Campbooks, LinkedIn). Who may create an account is the invite list, managed from the server's command line only.

tags.name: profile
tags.description: The master profile: what agents know about you. Imported from a LinkedIn data export, a PDF or pasted text as a draft you review, and edited by hand.

tags.name: pipeline
tags.description: Every opportunity in one place, from first match to offer: found by a search or added by link, with its stage, match, notes and next step. And Today: where you are and what to do next.

tags.name: sources
tags.description: The job search: public job boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Arbeitnow, HN Who is hiring) read and scored against your profile and goals, within the spending limits.

tags.name: bff
tags.description: The web app's backend-for-frontend: sign-in with a provider, the session cookie, sign-out. Browsers only.
